0000.note: The Rust kernel rewords some error messages; same errors otherwise (languages/l0000/CLAUDE.md, "The Rust implementation").

0003.note: Check errors name what was found more clearly ("the string \"dark\"" rather than "tag dark"); conformance compares them up to "Got" (languages/l0003/CLAUDE.md, "Conformance").
The TypeScript L0003 is on @graffiticode/l0000 0.8; the Rust kernel also has exact numbers and format-number, and serves those words (languages/l0003/CLAUDE.md, "Conformance").

0010.note: The TypeScript L0010 is on @graffiticode/l0000 0.8; the Rust kernel also has exact numbers and format-number (languages/l0010/CLAUDE.md, "Conformance").

0179.note: An upstream {data, errors} envelope is unwrapped by the Rust kernel: its fields are laid over the output and its params/limit read; TypeScript spreads the envelope itself (languages/l0179/CLAUDE.md, "Conformance"). Kept, not copied (P4 decision 2026-10-28).

0180.note: The TypeScript PROG spreads options.data raw, so an envelope's data and errors keys go into the item; the Rust kernel unwraps it and spreads the learner's response (languages/l0180/CLAUDE.md). Kept, not copied (P4 decision 2026-10-28).

0181.note: An upstream {data, errors} envelope is unwrapped by the kernel; the TypeScript merges the envelope itself (languages/l0181/CLAUDE.md). Kept, not copied (P4 decision 2026-10-28).

0183.note: The {data, errors} envelope is unwrapped however deep it nests (languages/l0183/CLAUDE.md, "Upstream data"). Kept, not copied (P4 decision 2026-10-28).

0185.note: An L0000 error inside a record's function is the Rust kernel's message, not the TypeScript kernel's (languages/l0185/CLAUDE.md, "Conformance").
